content.user_title: Request Focused Code Reviews Before Merging
content.value_statement: Late review feedback can delay releases and hide important defects. This skill guides Claude, Codex, or Claude Code to request structured reviews before work continues.
actual_capabilities: Defines when to request a review after tasks, features, fixes, and merges.
Shows how to capture base and head git SHAs for a focused diff.
Provides a reviewer prompt that compares implementation against requirements.
Organizes feedback into Critical, Important, and Minor issue groups.
Requires clear merge readiness assessment with reasoning.
Encourages fixing serious feedback before continuing development.
limitations: It does not run tests or inspect code without an active agent workflow.
Review quality depends on accurate requirements and git range inputs.
It does not replace human approval for regulated or high-risk systems.
It assumes the repository context is available to the reviewing agent.

use_cases.title: Check Feature Completion
use_cases.description: Request a review after building a feature to confirm it matches the plan and has enough tests.

use_cases.title: Validate Task Batches
use_cases.description: Review each completed batch in a larger plan before starting the next batch.

use_cases.title: Prepare for Merge
use_cases.description: Use the reviewer prompt to find blocking issues before a pull request reaches final approval.

prompt_templates.title: Review My Latest Change
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review request after one completed task.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the requesting-code-review skill to review my latest change. Compare the implementation with the task requirements and report Critical, Important, and Minor issues.

prompt_templates.title: Review a Git Range
prompt_templates.scenario: Focused review between two known commits.
prompt_templates.prompt: Request a code review for the range from BASE_SHA to HEAD_SHA. Check correctness, tests, architecture, and merge readiness.

prompt_templates.title: Review Against a Plan
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate review for a planned implementation.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the code-reviewer template to compare the completed work against this plan. Include file references, why each issue matters, and how to fix it.

prompt_templates.title: Gate a Major Merge
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced review before merging a larger feature.
prompt_templates.prompt: Run a production readiness review for this feature branch. Prioritize security, data loss, breaking changes, missing tests, and requirements gaps before giving a merge verdict.

output_examples.input: A developer asks for review after adding a verification function.
output_examples.output: The review lists strengths, one Important issue about missing progress feedback, one Minor cleanup, and a with-fixes merge assessment.

output_examples.input: An engineering lead reviews a completed task batch against a plan.
output_examples.output: The review confirms completed requirements, flags a test coverage gap, recommends a focused fix, and says whether work can continue.

output_examples.input: A release engineer requests a final pre-merge review.
output_examples.output: The review checks readiness, highlights any blocking risk, and gives a clear merge decision with short technical reasoning.

best_practices: Run the review after each meaningful task or feature, before new work depends on it.
Provide clear requirements, base SHA, head SHA, and a concise implementation summary.
Fix Critical and Important findings before continuing unless you can justify a technical exception.
anti_patterns: Do not ask for review without giving the reviewer a specific git range or requirement source.
Do not treat style comments as blockers when functional or security issues are absent.
Do not ignore valid review feedback because the change seems small.

faq.question: What does this skill review?
faq.answer: It guides an AI reviewer to compare code changes against requirements, tests, architecture, and production readiness.

faq.question: Does it run the review automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides the workflow and prompt structure for Claude, Codex, or Claude Code to request the review.

faq.question: What inputs should I provide?
faq.answer: Provide what changed, the relevant plan or requirements, the base SHA, the head SHA, and a short description.

faq.question: Can it replace a pull request review?
faq.answer: No. It is a preparation step that helps find issues before human or team review.

faq.question: How are issues prioritized?
faq.answer: The template separates findings into Critical, Important, and Minor groups based on actual impact.

faq.question: Is it useful when I am stuck?
faq.answer: Yes. A focused review can identify missing context, weak tests, or design problems that block progress.
